A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same KAN online-learning study. The complete main texts, equations, figures, tables and appendices support comparison; v2 expands Appendix B and adds Appendix D.

before.justification: v1 reports original experiments on drifting regression, synthetic qubit readout, randomized Acrobot and rotating digits, together with FPGA synthesis results.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experiments and adds baseline evaluations, initialization/normalization analyses and FPGA post-route validation results.

M1.justification: The proposed KAN retains precomputed spline-value/derivative LUTs, cached grid indices, sparse active-coefficient updates and fully on-chip training. The mathematical revisions do not establish a changed KAN procedure. Added initialization and normalization components belong to comparison MLPs.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same drifting regression, rotating Kerr-distorted IQ stream, randomized Acrobot, rotating UCI digits and input-dimension scaling scenarios. The added comparisons reuse existing tasks and data conditions.

E2.justification: v2 adds an evaluated OS-ELM comparator with 10 sigmoid hidden features for qubit readout in Table 1. Appendix D substantially expands comparisons with LSUV, LayerNorm and combined variants of both MLP-P and MLP-L on regression and qubit readout.

E3.justification: Appendix B.8 adds full placement, routing and timing analysis beyond v1's HLS synthesis estimates, retaining the 5 ns clock constraint. Appendix D introduces initialization/normalization controls and corresponding parameter budgets. Table 1 changes the reported qubit MLP precision from <10,3> to <7,3>, while the 10-bit configurations remain in Table 4; this does not establish that existing experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: Appendix D adds a substantial controlled study of whether initialization and normalization explain the MLP performance gap, including their hardware costs on two benchmarks. Appendix B.8 separately checks whether synthesized KAN schedules meet timing after routing. Existing precision, capacity and drift analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Both retain Acrobot mean-plus-standard-deviation reporting over seeds and Appendix C's fixed-seed statement. v2 adds no run counts, confidence intervals, significance tests or empirical uncertainty-estimation procedures.

E6.justification: v2 adds OS-ELM accuracy of 41.8%, extended MLP performance and hardware results, and post-route timing/resource results. Examples include regression regret of 39.5 for LSUV MLP-L versus 48.3 for vanilla MLP-L, and qubit MLP-L latency of 1,620 ns with LayerNorm versus 370 ns without it. Table 1 now tabulates 7-bit qubit MLP accuracies of 50.4% and 49.0%; v1's 10-bit 69.8% and 62.4% remain in Table 4, so these are not same-setting declines.

T1.justification: v1's Theorem 3.5 becomes Proposition 3.5, removing the quantization-error variance bounds and their Appendix A.3 derivation while retaining the gradient identities and bounded spline factor. Appendix A.1 also corrects the equal-budget setup by allowing distinct MLP and KAN dimensions. These substantively revise the formal justification, especially for quantization robustness.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same central claims: sparse spline-local updates, favorable capacity scaling, fixed-point robustness and the first model-free online learning at sub-microsecond latency. The added evidence supports these retained claims.

C2.justification: v2 replaces the future-work discussion of MLP normalization with interpretations of LSUV benefits, LayerNorm costs and fixed-point instability. It attributes poor OS-ELM performance to limited expressivity and revises the HLS limitation discussion using post-route validation. The existing streaming-SGD and scalability limitations remain.

D1.justification: Appendix B.8 adds Vivado 2024.1 and the implementation workflow. Appendix D documents offline LSUV initialization, LayerNorm placement, trainable affine parameters and float32 verification against PyTorch. Most existing implementation details remain, but v1's front-page ECLAIR repository link is removed without a replacement access link.

R1.justification: v2 adds Ba et al.'s Layer Normalization and Mishkin and Matas's initialization work, and expands positioning against stabilized MLPs and OS-ELM. The Related Works section and broader novelty positioning remain unchanged.

P1.justification: There are localized rewrites in the baseline and limitations discussions, revised theorem/proposition terminology, and new Appendix B.8 and Appendix D sections. The main section order and most prose remain intact.

P2.justification: v2 adds three appendix tables for post-route validation and extended MLP comparisons, inserts an OS-ELM row into Table 1 and extends Figure 3's caption. Existing figure graphics are retained. The original stream-parameter table becomes Table 3, with local reflow and relocation elsewhere.

improvement.justification: Post-route timing validation strengthens v1's reliance on HLS estimates, and explicit initialization/normalization controls address a previously deferred baseline concern. The corrected equal-budget setup also improves rigor. These gains are tempered by unreconciled precision wording between Tables 1 and 4, a claimed HLS/post-route resource match contradicted by Figure 3 and Table 2, and removal of the code-access link. Overall, the evidence becomes more credible, with reporting weaknesses limiting the improvement.
